newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - DEKALB, MYCOGEN BUYS REITERATED.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - DEKALB, MYCOGEN BUYS REITERATED.

text.p: Dain Bosworth analyst Bonnie Wittenburg said Friday she reiterated her buy ratings on agricultural and biotechnology companies DeKalb Genetics Corp and Mycogen Corp.
-- This followed DuPont Co's agreement on Thursday to purchase a 20 percent stake of Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc for $1.7 billion.

-- Wittenburg sid she believes the Pioneer-DuPont deal heightens the odds that DowElanco, a unit of Dow Chemical Co, would buy the rest of Mycogen, and that Monsanto Co would purchase the rest of DeKalb.
-- A Monsanto spokeswoman declined to comment, saying, "we never speculate on acquisition or divestiture rumors." A DowElanco spokesman was not immediately available.

-- DowElanco has a standstill agreement limiting its ownership in Mycogen to 65 percent until February 1999. "...(B)ut it is our opinion that DowElanco should be able to overcome that obstacle by offering a premium to whatever the stock price is at the moment," Wittenburg wrote.

-- Monsanto, which owns about 40 percent of DeKalb, has a 10-year standstill agreement. But Wittenburg said she believes DeKalb could still be sold if the Roberts family, which has majority control of DeKalb's voting shares, decided to do so.
-- "It is our belief that it strategically makes a lot of sense for Monsanto to own the rest of DeKalb, and the sooner the better," Wittenburg said.

-- "...(A)ctions such as the Pioneer-DuPont agreement make it clearer that it is very tough to remain independent unless one has very deep pockets," she added. "It is our opinion that DeKalb's pockets aren't deep enough for the long haul."
-- DeKalb shares were unchanged at 78-3/4. Mycogen shares were up 1/2 at 25.
